title: Circle Angles, Arcs, and Tangents
seo_title: Circle Angles Worksheet: Central, Inscribed Angles and Tangents (Geometry, G-C.A.2) | 100 Questions
standard_text: Identify and describe relationships among inscribed angles, radii, and chords. Include the relationship between central, inscribed, and circumscribed angles; inscribed angles on a diameter are right angles; the radius of a circle is perpendicular to the tangent where the radius intersects the circle.
meta_desc: Free Geometry worksheet on circle angles: central and inscribed angles, arcs, inscribed quadrilaterals, tangents, chords and secants. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: An inscribed angle is half its arc. A central angle equals its arc.
key_sub: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius. Opposite angles of an inscribed quadrilateral add to 180°.
body_html:
How it works

  • A central angle (vertex at the center) equals its arc. A circle is 360°, and a semicircle is 180°.
  • An inscribed angle (vertex on the circle) is half its intercepted arc. An angle inscribed in a semicircle is 90°.
  • Opposite angles of an inscribed quadrilateral are supplementary.
  • A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of tangency. Two tangent segments from the same outside point are congruent.
  • Two chords crossing inside: angle = ½(sum of arcs). Secants or tangents meeting outside: angle = ½(difference of arcs).
Example

An inscribed angle intercepts a 124° arc. Find the angle.

Half of 124°

Answer: 62°

Example

PA is tangent to circle O at A, OA = 6 and OP = 10. Find PA.

∠OAP = 90°

PA = √(100 − 36)

Answer: 8

Common mistakes

  • Giving an inscribed angle the same measure as its arc. Halve the arc.
  • Halving a central angle. Only inscribed angles are half the arc.
  • Adding opposite angles of an inscribed quadrilateral to 360°. They add to 180°.
  • Adding the arcs for an angle outside the circle. Subtract them, then halve.

faq.q: What is the inscribed angle theorem?
faq.a: An inscribed angle is half the measure of its intercepted arc.

faq.q: What is the difference between a central angle and an inscribed angle?
faq.a: A central angle has its vertex at the center and equals its arc. An inscribed angle has its vertex on the circle and is half its arc.

faq.q: Why is a tangent perpendicular to the radius?
faq.a: The radius to the point of tangency is the shortest distance from the center to the tangent line, and the shortest segment to a line is perpendicular.

faq.q: What are the angles of a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle?
faq.a: Opposite angles are supplementary: they add to 180 degrees.

items.q: PA is tangent to circle O at A. OA = 20 and PA = 21. Find OP.
items.e: OA ⟂ PA, so OP is the hypotenuse: √(20² + 21²) = 29.

items.q: PA is tangent to circle O at A. OA = 7 and OP = 25. Find PA.
items.e: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of tangency, so △OAP is a right triangle with hypotenuse OP. PA = √(25² − 7²) = 24.

items.q: Two chords intersect inside a circle. The arcs intercepted by the angle and its vertical angle measure 128° and 118°. Find the angle.
